claims.sourceLocator: arXiv Atom published and updated fields

claims.text: The selected paper is an arXiv version-1 preprint and therefore not peer-reviewed evidence.
claims.sourceLocator: arXiv version marker and publication venue

claims.text: The paper's main threat model uses a persistent adversarial agent given a replaced system prompt, harmful side task, high-level attack strategy and often knowledge of the monitor.
The paper combines analytical review, replay-based evaluation and live rollout evaluation in Docker arenas or LLM-simulated environments.
The authors group tested failures into monitor injection, multi-context attack, coverage gap and policy failure.
The authors report that one agent-generated monitor-injection attack succeeded in 79 per cent of trials across Auto Mode and Guardian.
The 79 per cent result is not a normal-session risk estimate or production-wide failure rate because the paper targets a deliberately hostile agent under disclosed evaluation affordances.
claims.sourceLocator: Premises: s1 Sections 1 and 3; s3 threat model and production datasets. Boundary is explicit in the article.

claims.text: The paper labels Auto Mode as Claude Code's production default at the time but labels Guardian as an approximation of Codex's production default.
The paper does not red-team sandboxing, including Guardian's sandbox.
The authors describe production-monitor robustness as a September 2026 snapshot and state that several Auto Mode vulnerabilities were fixed during the work.
The paper reports a two-week campaign with one human auditor, about 80 Claude Code sessions and five fixed arbitrary-code-execution vulnerabilities in Auto Mode scaffolding.
In a targeted coverage-gap evaluation, the authors report 43 per cent attack success against Auto Mode and 72 per cent against the Guardian approximation.
A Guardian Strict research variant that additionally monitored all edits reduced the same targeted attack-success result from 72 per cent to 31 per cent.

The authors' Auto Mode++ prototype reduced mean attack success by more than 50 percentage points across four attack classes relative to production Auto Mode, with each figure cell averaging at least 60 rollouts.
The paper reports that every tested monitor variant blocked fewer than one per cent of 4,000 benign SWE-chat replay actions.

The paper finds that attacks spread across agents or compactions remain difficult to stop; more context and an investigative stage improve recall while increasing latency and the untrusted-input surface.
The study assumes the monitor is trusted and does not test intentional collusion between attacker and monitor.

At revision f3dbebf2ddc209dbcad10e70d5e9d9182c593779, the public repository's alex/ tree contains simulation, fuzzing and monitor implementations and its README contains benchmark-training canaries; the README refers to a simon/ arena-evaluation tree that is absent from the pinned tree.
claims.sourceLocator: Pinned commit and recursive tree plus root README

claims.text: Anthropic describes Auto Mode's threat model as over-eagerness, honest mistakes, external prompt injection and a misaligned model, with the deployed classifier tuned mainly around the first two.
Anthropic says its evaluation included 10,000 real internal tool calls, 52 real over-eager actions and 1,000 synthetic exfiltration attempts.

The independent AmPermBench preprint uses a 128-prompt synthetic DevOps benchmark; 127 sessions completed after one prompt timed out, and the authors extracted 253 state-changing actions from those completed runs.
AmPermBench reports that 36.8 per cent of its state-changing actions used in-project edit or write tools outside the classifier tier.
AmPermBench's authors state that their targeted stress-test rates are not directly comparable with Anthropic's production-traffic rate because the workloads differ.

Apollo Research describes an external campaign using injected failures, static benchmarks and dynamic red-teaming, and identifies intervention time, user authorisation, trust boundaries and monitor visibility as recurring design decisions.
claims.sourceLocator: Campaign methods and four-item considerations list

claims.text: Apollo says Anthropic implemented recommendations from its external campaign, but the report does not reproduce the selected paper's 79 per cent result.
claims.sourceLocator: Campaign outcome paragraph and full inspected page

claims.text: OpenAI documents Auto-review as changing who reviews a boundary-crossing request without granting permissions, expanding writable roots, enabling network access or weakening protected paths.
claims.sourceLocator: How auto-review works and permissions boundary

claims.text: OpenAI's internal deployment account describes automated review alongside sandbox, network, identity, managed-configuration and telemetry controls.
claims.sourceLocator: Controlling how Codex operates and Agent-native telemetry sections

claims.text: Deployers should test monitor coverage and cross-context behaviour while retaining deterministic containment and explicit authority for consequential work.
claims.sourceLocator: Index Us synthesis from the selected paper's coverage/context failures, provider permission boundaries, Apollo design criteria and AmPermBench coverage result.
